one_month_reasoning: The main event in the window is Microsoft's fiscal Q1 2027 earnings, expected about Oct 27-28, 2026 after the close (date not yet confirmed, so it lands before the Oct 30 scoring close). Management guided revenue of $89.85-90.95B, Azure +45% cc and capex above $50B for the quarter; FY27 EPS consensus is about $4.72 for Q1. The stock has run from a ~$349 low to $518, near a 10-month high, on the Copilot relaunch and a Stifel upgrade, so the bar is high. The skeptic risks for the print are capex above $50B, a lower capex-to-revenue payoff, and any softening of OpenAI-linked bookings, weighed against a guide that is usually beaten. I see no edge on the direction, so the distribution is centred on today's price. It uses monthly sigma of about 9.5% (32%/3.5 = 9.1%, widened slightly for the earnings gap), with a bit of extra tail mass on both sides.

fair_value.method: Blend of 70% P/E (skeptic FY28 EPS $21.50 x 24x = $516) and 30% FCF yield (FY28 FCF ~$85B at a 2.75% yield, 7.43B shares = $412), giving about $485 as the fair value a year out.

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus FY27 $19.76 grown at ~14% would give ~$22.5 for FY28. I cut about 4.5% because D&A ($39B in FY26) has to catch up with capex ($116B in FY26, >$50B per quarter now). The sec-api analysis projects depreciation rising from 11.6% to 16.7% of revenue by FY29. The 15-to-25-year useful-life change for buildings and the shift to operating leases flatter reported D&A, and I treat that as low quality rather than as earnings.

The stock is on ~26x FY27 consensus today ($518/$19.76). July PT cuts (Citi, Mizuho) cited software-wide multiple compression. Capex at ~35% of revenue (vs 23% before) and falling FCF justify a turn or two below today, and that is a discount to the ~28-30x the stock carried in 2023-25.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY2028 FCF ~$85B / 2.75% yield = $3.09T; less ~$30B net debt incl. finance leases; / 7.43B diluted shares

inputs_detail.input: FY2026 operating cash flow / capex / FCF

inputs_detail.derivation: sec-api analysis of the FY26 10-K: finance lease liabilities of $66.6B take the balance sheet from +$5.2B net cash to about -$30B net debt

OCF grows ~17% a year to about $250B. Capex is ~$160-170B (Q1 FY27 guide >$50B per quarter, CY26 ~$175B). The shift to operating leases moves some spend into OCF, so I use about $85B rather than the headline gap.
Around MSFT's historic 2.5-3% FCF yield. AAA credit and near-Treasury spreads argue against a larger discount, but AI-debt supply is widening sector spreads (~115bp), so I do not use a premium yield.

bear.story: OpenAI (~$24B, 7% of FY26 revenue; ~1/3 of the $678B backlog) has trouble raising the capital it needs to keep burning cash, or moves spend to other clouds under the loosened April-2026 terms. Azure falls toward 30%, capex is already committed and depreciation eats into margins, while HLBV equity losses return. FY28 EPS comes in around $18.5 and the multiple falls to ~19-20x, back toward the $349 low.

base.story: Azure grows 35-40% while capacity constrained. Copilot seat growth offsets a gradual rise in depreciation, and EPS grows low-to-mid teens to ~$21.5-22. The multiple drifts down slightly to ~24x, so the price is roughly flat to slightly up.

bull.story: Copilot bundling lifts Office ARPU, the backlog converts on time, OpenAI IPOs strongly (Polymarket prices a >$1T listing by 2027 as likely), the equity stake is marked up and concentration fears fade. EPS reaches ~$24 at 28-29x.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$400 (about -23%, under the post-earnings April-May range, and 20x FY27 consensus) the move would most likely reflect a fundamental break rather than volatility. The likely cause is OpenAI cutting or delaying Azure commitments (32% of RPO), an Azure deceleration below 30%, or a capex guide that keeps rising while revenue guidance falls, which would signal an impaired return on the ~$175B/yr build.

reasoning: Reported base: FY26 revenue $331.8B (+18%), non-GAAP EPS $17.28, Azure +43%, and Q1 FY27 guided Azure +45%. The bear case has substance. (1) Concentration: OpenAI was $24.1B of revenue and roughly a third of the $678B commercial RPO; ex-OpenAI, backlog grew 25% versus 84% headline. OpenAI burns cash and in April 2026 won the right to use any cloud. (2) Earnings quality: capex runs at ~3x D&A. Microsoft just extended building lives from 15 to 25 years and is shifting data-center leases to operating treatment, which moved ~$15B out of the capex guide without changing spending. That echoes the Burry critique that hyperscaler earnings are overstated, and depreciation could reach ~17% of revenue by FY29. FCF has fallen two years in a row to $67B while the company went from net cash to ~$30B net debt including finance leases, with $329B of uncommenced leases. (3) Sell-side trimmed targets in July (Citi 620 to 570, Mizuho 515 to 490) on multiple compression, not on the business. Weighing it honestly: credit is pristine (AAA; bonds near Treasuries; least funding need of the hyperscalers per BofA), and insider selling is routine (Nadella's $43M 10b5-1 sale, still holding 487k shares). There are 0 Sells among 55 analysts (avg PT $577, low $440), so the consensus is crowded long, which is itself a skeptic's point. My fair value of ~$485 is below spot. The distribution is a mixture: 80% lognormal (median ~$525, sigma 0.27) plus a 20% bear component (median ~$380, sigma 0.25) for an OpenAI or AI-capex unwind. That gives P(>=518) of about 0.44, a median of about $500 and a fatter left tail than a symmetric 32%-vol lognormal. Research used ~12 searches and 5 fetches. X/Twitter was not tried. The Polymarket resolution rules were not visible in the fetch.
